---
title: "Part 4 – Multiverse, replication and preregistration"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/housing-one-day-methods.html#/part-4-multiverse-replication-and-preregistration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 4 opens on the chart that the class has just built and reads it against every justifiable analysis of the claim on these data. It then leaves the original data behind for the replication that SCORE ran with new emails, and it closes on the single analysis that you would defend, declared before it runs.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Multiverse](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd) and slides | Your own small multiverse, then the curve of the claim: the 64 specifications ranked from the largest gap to the smallest, with the published result of the original authors (OAs) and the five analysts placed on it. An optional pair of slides tells where the idea of a multiverse came from and draws the garden of forking paths. | 10 minutes |
| [Multiverse](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd#class-results) | Find your own mark among the exploratory results of the class. Then rerun `try_spec()` with the choices that you submitted and read your placement, the number of the 64 specifications whose gap lies further below zero than yours, and send it in chat when the facilitator says go. | 10 minutes |
| Slides | What moved the estimate: each option of the curve set beside its twins, and the step in the curve that comes from the choice of which emails to count. | 6 minutes |
| Slides, with [the replication](../../cases/housing/index.qmd#sec-replication) on the case study as the follow-up | The SCORE replication, a preregistered audit of 3,050 housing authorities with new names; what it found; the original study and the replication compared row by row; the power of the two designs; the three Rs on this paper; and what separates robustness from replicability. | 14 minutes |
| Slides, with [The multiverse and its critics](../../companion/multiverse.qmd) as the follow-up | The critics of the multiverse, the argument that a fully specified question has one correct analysis and how anyone would identify it, what preregistration settles and what it leaves open, and the difference between the exploration of Task 4 and the declaration of Task 5. | 10 minutes |
| Slides, with [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd) as the follow-up | Where a reanalysis is archived and registered, the preregistration of Multi100 itself, the two preregistration templates, the public record of the case with a three-minute search of the replication report, and the eight AsPredicted questions mapped onto the decisions that you have already met. | 10 minutes |
| [Browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-5-preregistration) Task 5, or the preregistration block in your report | Complete the preregistration block before you run anything: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, one option for each decision, a sentence from your causal graph on why the specification answers the claim, and your rule for what supports or undermines it. On the browser lab page copy the completed cell into your notes, or render the report, and type "declared" in chat. When the class has declared, fit the specification with `run_spec()` and send it with `report_result()`. Your declared result is drawn on the chart as a filled circle beside the open circles of Task 4. | 22 minutes |
| Slides and [Multiverse](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd#class-results) | Two points from the literature, the single analytical path, what you take with you and the feedback form, with the class chart on screen. | 8 minutes |

**By the end of the part** you have your own placement among the 64 specifications of the curve, one specification fixed in the preregistration block of your report before it was run, a report of your own that contains the result of that specification, and a view of what a result that holds under every analysis of one sample does and does not say about new data.
